facts.statement: Orientognathus is a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic of China.
facts.quote: Orientognathus is a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic of China.

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single specimen containing most of the skeleton and skull, which was first named and described in 2015 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen which includes most of the skeleton and skull, and was first named and described in 2015 by Lü Junchang et al..

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Upper Jurassic Tuchengzi Formation of China, a layer slightly younger than the Tiaojishan Formation where other regional pterosaurs are found.
facts.quote: The taxon was found in the Upper Jurassic Tuchengzi Formation of China, which is slightly younger than the Tiaojishan Formation that most other Middle Jurassic pterosaurs from the region have been found in.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis determined that Orientognathus was a basal member of the family Rhamphorhynchidae, possibly belonging to the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: The description study produced a phylogenetic analysis, which determined that Orientognathus was a basal member of Rhamphorhynchidae, possibly within Rhamphorhynchinae.

facts.statement: Orientognathus is an extinct basal pterosaur that lived in the Late Jurassic in the area of modern-day China.
facts.quote: Orientognathus es un género extinto de pterosaurio basal ("ranforincoideo") que vivió a finales del Jurásico en el área de la actual China.

facts.statement: The species Orientognathus chaoyangensis was named and described in 2015 by Lü Junchang, Hanyong Pu, Xu Li, Wei Xufang, Huali Chang, and Martin Kundrát.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue nombrado y descrito en 2015 por Lü Junchang, Hanyong Pu, Xu Li, Wei Xufang, Huali Chang y Martin Kundrát, con la especie tipo Orientognathus chaoyangensis.

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the Latin word oriens, referring to its origin in East Asia, and the Ancient Greek word gnathos, meaning "jaw".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del término en latín oriens, en referencia a su procedencia del oriente de Asia, y el término en griego antiguo γνάθος, gnathos, "mandíbula".

facts.statement: The species name refers to the location where the fossil was found, Chaoyang.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a haber sido encontrado en Chaoyang.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, 41HIII-0418, was found in western Liaoning province within the Tuchengzi Formation, dated to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: El ejemplar holotipo, 41HIII-0418, fue hallado en el oeste de la provincia de Liaoning, en una capa de la Formación Tuchengzi la cual ha sido datada de la época del Titoniense del Jurásico Superior, unos 150 millones de años.

facts.statement: The toothless front of the lower jaw is slightly pointed.
facts.quote: El frente sin dientes de la mandíbula inferior está ligeramente apuntado.

facts.statement: The fourth metacarpal bone is 38% of the length of the humerus.
facts.quote: El cuarto hueso metacarpiano tiene 38% de la longitud del húmero.

facts.statement: The ulna is shorter than any of the wing phalanges.
facts.quote: El cúbito es más corto que cualquier falange del ala.

facts.statement: The tibia is almost as long as the femur.
facts.quote: La tibia es casi tan largo como el fémur.

facts.statement: The teeth of Orientognathus are straight, relatively robust, and long.
facts.quote: En Orientognathus los dientes son rectos y relativamente robustos y largos.

facts.statement: The pteroid wing bone is 21% of the length of the humerus and has an expanded tip.
facts.quote: El hueso pteroide del ala tiene un 21% de la longitud del húmero y tiene un extremo ensanchado.

facts.statement: The deltopectoral crest on the humerus is not very developed.
facts.quote: La cresta deltopectoral en el húmero no está muy desarrollada.

facts.statement: Orientognathus is included in the family Rhamphorhynchidae and more specifically within the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: Orientognathus ha sido incluido en la familia Rhamphorhynchidae, y más específicamente dentro de la subfamilia Rhamphorhynchinae.

facts.statement: It is the largest known Rhamphorhynchinae from the Late Jurassic of China and the only known pterosaur from the Tithonian of that country.
facts.quote: Constituye el mayor Rhamphorhynchinae conocido del Jurásico Superior de China y el único pterosaurio conocido del Titoniano de ese país.

facts.statement: The parent group of Orientognathus is Rhamphorhynchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rhamphorhynchinae

facts.statement: Orientognathus belongs to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Rhamphorhynchidae

facts.statement: The time range for Orientognathus is the Berriasian, from 143.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Berriasian (143.1 to 137.05 million years ago)
